settings.hero_badge: Student Researcher & Technology Builder in Robotics, Environmental & Biomedical Engineering
settings.hero_bio: My vision is a world where clean water and basic health care reach communities too often overlooked—and I want to build tools that help make that possible. My work brings together responsible AI, robotics, hands-on engineering, and science in service of communities, guided by the belief that the hardest problems in equity are never just technical. Whether I’m developing a biochar water remediation system, modeling cancer-signaling networks, building a phone-based vital signs app, or writing a poem that gives feelings a form, I return to the same question: How can we make care more honest, more equitable, and more accessible?
settings.invite_body: Aadya is available to speak at student events, mentor young women entering STEM, and collaborate on water, responsible-AI and equitable-health research. Reach out to arrange a conversation.

portfolio.title: MIT Solve — AI for a Better World
portfolio.desc: One of five national winners of MIT Solve AI for a Better World Challenge; presented an AI-powered water-quality node at the MIT Media Lab.  My Journey started with testing water quality. I spent several months in the lab testing how softwood- and agricultural-waste-based biochar pulls contaminants out of water, then asked what it would take to put that science in the hands of communities that need it. The answer became Project RHINE, an AI- and IoT-informed monitoring and treatment concept that pairs low-cost sensors, data analysis, and biochar filtration. MIT Solve named RHINE one of the five national winners of its AI for A Better World Youth Innovation Global Challenge. The research earned regional U.S. Stockholm Junior Water Prize recognition and a NOAA “Taking the Pulse of the Planet” award, and I presented it at the New Jersey Water Environment Association conference and the IEEE ISEC Conference at Princeton University. My manuscript is now under peer review at the Journal of Emerging Investigators.
highlights: One of five national MIT Solve AI for a Better World winners

Pairs water-quality sensing with edge machine learning and actionable treatment response

portfolio.title: Biochar Water Treatment
portfolio.desc: Bench tests comparing waste-derived biochars for water remediation, collected 900+ data points from water treatment lab experiments (varying dosage, pH, and contact times) and conducted statistical analysis using Mann-Whitney U and Spearman’s rank correlation methods. portfolio.title: Biomedical & AI Scientific Research
portfolio.desc:
Research and Training Experience

1. Molecular and Cellular Biology — Coursework and Wet-Lab Training
Completed a 24-week molecular and cellular biology program with Professor Sam Kunes of Harvard University, followed by three weeks of summer wet-lab training. Studied Alzheimer’s disease, molecular mechanisms, experimental design, controls, and laboratory methods.

2. Computational Biology and Cancer Research — Independent Projects

Conducting computational research to investigate cancer biology and develop testable hypotheses:

Single-cell RNA sequencing: Used Python for data normalization, dimensionality reduction, and clustering.

Cancer signaling: Developing graph-theory and Boolean-network models of cancer signaling.

Cervical cancer: Completed an initial computational phase using molecular docking and simulations to generate hypotheses. Planning a second phase involving wet-lab experiments and transcriptomic analysis to evaluate potential biological effects and underlying mechanisms.

These projects are exploratory and ongoing; they do not establish clinical efficacy or treatment discoveries.

3. Stanford AIMI — 30-Week Academic-Year Research Internship

Participating as an academic-year machine-learning researcher on “User-Centric AI for Assisting the Visually Impaired,” a project integrating neuroimaging and AI. Gaining experience in accessibility, model validation, and user-centered design in health technology.
highlights: Machine Learning & AI: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN), Random Forest, XGBoost, Predictive Modeling, Data Cleansing, Imbalance Resolution.
Programming & Software: Python, MATLAB, Google Colab, Bash Scripting.
Bioinformatics Tools: AutoDock Vina (Molecular Docking), Computational Structural Biology, Protein Modeling, Graph Theory Networks.
Wet Lab Techniques: Sterile cell culture, CRISPR-Cas9 protocols, gel electrophoresis, PCR preparation, chemical safety.
Stanford AIMI Clinical AI: Selected for competitive 30-week internship (<5% acceptance rate), developing computer vision assistive interfaces utilizing medical imaging.
Computational Oncology: Co-authoring manuscript on cervical cancer treatments using AutoDock Vina molecular docking simulations.
Biomedical Research Fellow (Harvard Mentor Prof. Sam Kunes): 24-week bioresearch program with 3 weeks hands-on wet lab work in Boston (CRISPR, gel electrophoresis, PCR).
Independent Cancer Research (Cambridge Mentor Dr. Kristina Kordova): scRNA-seq analysis & Python classification model identifying 32 breast cancer biomarker clusters.

etymology.title: What "Aadya" Means to Me
etymology.content: My name is rooted in ancient Sanskrit (आद्या), meaning "The First" and "The Primordial". In Indian tradition, it represents intentional agency, calm resilience, and the quiet responsibility to act before others do. To me, it has never meant finishing first in an easy race. It means being willing to take the very first step into uncomfortable, unpaved problems—whether that's diagnosing heavy-metal contamination in agricultural runoff or stepping up to code complex odometry splines under competition pressure.

quote.text: Nothing beats kindness. It sits quietly beyond all things.
quote.author: CHARLIE MACKESY, THE BOY, THE MOLE, THE FOX AND THE HORSE
quote.reflection: In high-velocity engineering, it's dangerously easy to obsess solely over performance—PID loops, velocity constraints, or sensor parts-per-million. This quote is my compass: technical rigor is hollow if it doesn't leave people feeling treated with gentleness and dignity.

about.lead_bio: Student Researcher and Technology builder — working where responsible AI, hands-on engineering and community science meet, so that clean water and basic care reach the people the world usually forgets.
about.story_p1: Aadya Agarwal is a Princeton, New Jersey student with roots in India. Her name comes from Sanskrit — it means “first” and “excellent,” and echoes the goddess Durga, a symbol of primordial energy and power. She grew up in a lively, multicultural home where unstructured conversation was the norm, and that upbringing shaped how she works: curious across disciplines, quick to include people, and grateful for the relationships that carry an idea forward.
about.story_p2: Her favorite book is Charlie Mackesy’s The Boy, the Mole, the Fox and the Horse, which keeps her anchored to a simple goal — to live with gratitude and leave the world a little better than she found it. That outlook runs through everything from her water-remediation research to equitable healthcare to the poems she writes.
about.story_p3: Away from the lab and the page, Aadya is an enthusiastic adventurer and cook. She has gone parasailing, horseback riding and skiing, spent time on farms, and once — at age ten — made a 20-foot cliff jump into the crystal-clear water of a Mexican cenote. In the kitchen she likes to experiment, including an avocado buttercream she is quietly proud of.
about.glance_intro: A student drawn to questions that cross disciplines — engineering and environmental research alongside writing, public speaking, music and community service.

about.takeaways_intro: Aadya hopes her path is useful to other students — especially young women — who are deciding whether their questions are worth chasing. A few things she has learned along the way:

takeaways.title: Start before you feel ready.
takeaways.desc: Aadya’s projects began as questions she did not yet know how to answer — a water sample, a sensor, a first line of code — and grew through iteration, not certainty.

takeaways.title: Let disciplines cross.
takeaways.desc: Her strongest work lives where engineering meets environmental science, writing and community service; the most interesting problems rarely stay inside one subject.

takeaways.title: Build for the people usually left out.
takeaways.desc: Whether it is a one-minute vitals check at a farmers market or a low-cost water filter or decoding the language of hidden diseases, the goal is to make care and opportunity more within reach.

about.invite_headline: Invite Aadya to speak or collaborate
about.invite_body: Aadya is glad to speak at student events and panels, mentor young women entering STEM, and collaborate on research in water, responsible AI and equitable health. If her work resonates — or you would like her to share it with your students or team — reach out and she will be happy to arrange a conversation.
